claims.text: The evidence shows that source 183.62.140.253 generated a total of 580 log lines, whereas source 187.141.143.180 produced only 189 lines; this disparity indicates that the former attempted many more distinct credential checks before being terminated.

In both groups the attacker repeatedly tried to authenticate as “invalid user” or “root,” received a “Received disconnect … Bye Bye [preauth]” message, and then moved on to another failed attempt, confirming a cadence of rapid, repeated login probes that ended in disconnection rather than successful access.

Because the larger volume of attempts from 183.62.140.253 demonstrates a broader brute‑force sweep across many usernames, it is the more anomalous attacker when judged against its stated total_matching_lines.

A plausible root‑cause hypothesis is that an automated script or botnet was scanning for exposed SSH services and exhaustively enumerating possible accounts from 183.62.140.253, while the smaller set from 187.141.143.180 may represent a more targeted, opportunistic test of default credentials on a different host.
